meta.title: Analysis
meta.note: Findings drawn across the consolidated dataset. Each row states what the evidence supports, how strong it is, and links the source it rests on. Rows marked 'owner-provided' rest on information supplied by the requester and cannot be verified from any official source; they are never presented as verified.

rows.topic: Which licences can hold the whole job on one contract
rows.finding: Six of the 22 licences checked hold both B General Building and C-36 Plumbing, so a single contract can cover the plumbing and the drywall open-and-patch under BPC §7057(b): Ace Plumbing & Rooter #829071, We Do Construction #1096552, Rapid Flow #1115649, Save-On-Interior #749536, Ayoob & Peery #392967 and D G Construction #297604. Ace and Ayoob & Peery also hold fire-protection and HVAC classifications on the same licence.

rows.topic: The three quoting companies cannot do the drywall on their own licences
rows.finding: Expert Plumbing Solutions #977638, Bay Area Plumbing #757796 and Fast Response #1024971 are each C-36 only — no B and no C-9 drywall classification on their licences. Unless one of them brings a separately licensed contractor, the 'all in one service' requirement is not met by the three firms that have already quoted. Bay Area Plumbing's operator does hold a second licence (Save-On-Interior #749536) that carries B + C-36 at the same address and phone, which is the closest single-operator route among the quotees.

rows.topic: One licence in the set is suspended and must be excluded now
rows.finding: Kenneth Asire Plumbing #1027286 shows 'License is under suspension … Contractors Bond Suspension' with the contractor's bond cancelled on 16 August 2026. CSLB explains the suspension lifts retroactively once a bond is processed, so this is a re-check item, not a permanent exclusion — but do not contract while the page shows suspension.

rows.topic: One shortlisted licence carries published complaint-disclosure information
rows.finding: D G Construction Co #297604 is current and active and holds B + C-36, but its CSLB page displays 'There is Complaint Disclosure information for this license.' Read that record before contacting the firm; the disclosure content itself is not reproduced here.

rows.topic: Seven licences are addressed outside San Francisco
rows.finding: Fifteen of the 22 licence addresses of record are in San Francisco. Seven are elsewhere: SF Building Group #1106131 (South San Francisco), Discount Plumbing Rooter Services #1140843 and Caccia Home Services #379364 (Burlingame), Flow Masters #966337, FDL Plumbing #1086935 and Citywide Plumbing #954385 (Daly City) and Clever Plumbing & Rooter #1160613 (San Bruno). CSLB records the licence address, not a service area, so whether any of them works in San Francisco is unverified and must be asked directly.

rows.topic: A San Francisco permit is required before pipe is cut or covered — check the §104.2 exemption
rows.finding: DBI's official page says a permit is needed before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes that will be covered by a wall, and points to the exemption list in SF Plumbing Code §104.2. A waste-and-overflow replacement is exactly that kind of pipe work. The same page lists the licence classes that may apply (A; B after scope approval; C4/C36; C16; C20; C54), and notes that contractors registered for Express Permits on PermitSF skip staff review. The permit determination for this specific scope has not been obtained — ask the Permit Center help desk, 628-652-4900.

source_links.label: sf.gov — Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (DBI)

rows.topic: The three estimates cover three different jobs
rows.finding: $135 adjusts the plunger handle, $550 replaces the lever/plug/spout with a diverter, and $614 replaces the waste and overflow. None of them prices opening and patching the storage-unit ceiling, which is the step the below-access route adds. The amounts are owner-provided and cannot be checked against any official source, so they are published as unverified and are not ranked.

source_links.label: Project brief — owner-provided estimates dated 2026-08-30 (data file)

rows.topic: Removal from above is the manufacturer's documented service path
rows.finding: The manufacturer's installation sheet for a trip-lever bath waste reaches the linkage and drop cylinder through the overflow opening — its own service step is to remove the overflow plate and lift out the cylinder assembly. Nothing in the documented sequence requires opening a wall. That makes the 'from above' attempt worth re-asking, even though the requester reports five or more plumbers declined it.

source_links.label: Watco — Trip Lever Bath Waste installation instructions (manufacturer PDF)

rows.topic: If the ceiling is opened, the code asks for an access opening
rows.finding: The California Plumbing Code requires access to concealed slip-joint connections (12-inch minimum access opening; CPC §402.10 in the 2022 edition, renumbered from §404.2 in the 2010 edition). Patching the ceiling solid and refusing an access panel creates the same access problem again for the next repair.

rows.topic: Workers'-compensation status varies across the set
rows.finding: Eight of the 22 licences are recorded by CSLB as exempt from workers' compensation because the holder certified it has no employees: #757796, #749536, #1115649, #1106131, #297604, #961218, #954385 and #1160613. For an occupied building that is worth knowing before work starts, because anyone else on site would have to carry their own coverage.

rows.topic: One bond/WC dates need re-checking close to the job date
rows.finding: Fast Response Plumbing & Rooter #1024971 carries a workers'-compensation policy expiring 18 December 2026, and Advanced Plumbing and Drain #1009195 carries CSLB's 'Additional Status' warning that the licence may be suspended at a future date for an unresolved final liability. Both are current today; both should be re-read on the CSLB page on the day a contract is signed.

rows.topic: Tenant notice is a notice-rule, not a courtesy
rows.finding: Civil Code §1954 allows entry to make necessary or agreed repairs but requires written notice of the date, approximate time and purpose, during normal business hours unless the tenant consents at the time. Twenty-four hours is presumed reasonable notice, six days if mailed.

rows.topic: No provider in the verified set holds a C-9 drywall classification
rows.finding: None of the 22 licences carries C-9 (drywall). The drywall side of a below-access route is therefore covered either by a B or B-2 licence acting as prime contractor (see A-01) or by a separately licensed drywall contractor named in the same contract.
